steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cut an X in the bottom of the stems of the broccoli rabe and place in the boiling water. Cook until just tender but still firm, about 3 to 5 minutes. Drain.

In a large heavy skillet over medium heat, heat olive oil and sauté garlic for 1 to 2 minutes. Stir in the broccoli rabe and sauté for 8 to 10 minutes, or until desired doneness. Sprinkle with parmesan cheese, if desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Maria's Broccoli Rabe
raw_recipe.description: This sautéed broccoli rabe recipe with garlic and Parmesan cheese makes a super simple, colorful side dish that's elegant enough for company.
raw_recipe.name: Maria's Broccoli Rabe

review.reviewBody: I read one of the responses to this recipe about not boiling the broccoli rabe. Boiling it is a must. My grandmom was from Italy and made broccoli rabe all the time. She would definitely boil it and the stems are supposed to be soft. Everytime my dad and I eat broccoli rabe somewhere he constantly complains if the stems are hard. It ruins the broccoli rabe. It is usually not a bright green color. It is more of a dark color. Take my advice!!

Love this recipe but changed it slightly. I cut off the large ends of the broccoli rabe and then chop up the leaves, florettes and the thin stems. I then blanch the rapi and drain under cold water. I heat just a little olive oil in a pan and add mega amounts of garlic (sometimes 7 or 8 cloves minced) to 2 or 3 heads of broccoli rabe. Saute garlic for about 1 minute then add rapi to pan, stir around with garlic, then add 1 or 2 cans of cannellini beans (don't drain) and cook for a few minutes until hot. No need to add salt. Add some pepper, sprinkle a little parmesan stravechio and you've got a great meal. I eat this on a weekly basis whenever I can buy broccoli rabe. The absolute best.

Broccoli rabe is an acquired taste, even for native Italians (my dad is from Naples and mom is from Trieste - neither of whom would touch the stuff until I cooked it my way). The recipe submitted is basic but can be enhanced this way. Trim the ends of the stems. Bring a large pot or saucepan filled with salted water to a boil. Immerse the BR and cook for no more than 8 minutes. Drain immediately, flash chill and then spread on cookie sheet to continue cool down. The BR will be bright green yet tender. Cut the BR into bite size pieces. Saute some garlic to taste and a few hot pepper flakes in olive oil - about 3 tbsp. should do it. Then add BR, toss to coat and remove from heat when warmed through; you don't want to lose that beautiful bright green color. Place on a serving plate, top with a squirt of lemon juice and maybe some homemade toasted breadcrumbs. Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil and enjoy.

Oh this was good. Followed comments by Trixie (flash boil and cool, cut into pieces and saute in olive oil and garlic and sprinkle with toasted homemade bread crumbs)and it was the best broccoli rabe ever without sausage or pasta. Served with toasted Italian bread rubbed with garlic and drizzled EVOO and melted fresh mozzarella on top. Very filling meal and healthy.

I probably make this once a week and sometimes I serve it over fresh pasta. I always add chili peppers and salt (but I like my rapini on the salty side). It is absolutely delicious. On the topic of boiling it first...I have done it both ways and much prefer NOT to boil the rapini first. I find if it is boiled it takes on a completely different (less favourable) flavour. I never have trouble with the stems being tough because I cook it in the oil for a good amount of time (approximately 10 minutes.

I agree that rapini is hard to find but if you're lucky enough to have a "Sprouts" in your town you can always find it there. 

I believe this recipe would be good with brocolini but there's nothing like the taste of broccoli rabe. It's not something that everyone will like because it does have a strong (some say bitter) taste but but I believe that's why I love it so much. Five year olds may want to pass on it, but if your adults haven't tried it you're missing a real treat.

This recipe was delicious.

UPDATE:

For an ultra-delicious dinner, 
Saute some anchovies in a saucepan, since I love them I add a full can of them. Saute until they're dissolved. Add rapini and heat through. Toss with any kind of pasta and you'll be licking the plate.

Hints: Don't skimp on the Garlic and if you previously used EVOO to saute the broccoli rabe, use some butter to saute and melt the anchovies. After tossing the broccoli rabe with the rest of the ingredients (you did add some red pepper flakes, right?) sprinkle with some freshly grated Parmesan 

You're welcome ( if you're a broccoli rabe and anchovy lover.) Otherwise, please disregard this post.

I used this recipe as a base but with the following changes. 

First, I took the skin off the stems and I boiled them for 2 minutes at the most. With the skins off you don't need to boil it for long. 
I cooled the rabe immediately after taking it from the boiling water. I used continuously flowing tap water instead of ice water. 
I found another recipe that called for throwing away garlic after it releases the flavor but I like it fried too much so after 1 min I took it off the skillet and put it aside on paper towel, to spread it over the finished rabe after frying it a bit. I think if I left it in a skillet, even for another minute it would have burned.
And then, I didn't really fried the rabe, but rather made sure that the oil with the garlic flavor and salt (I added it to the oil) is spread over it, and that's it. Basically a minute while continuously stirring it. 
I didn't add any cheese but the fried garlic made all the difference! Too bad rabe is seasonal or I'd make it all year long.

I have tried everything to avoid blanching the rabe prior to cooking - steaming in the microwave, adding cooking time, adding liquid to the sauté pan to steam it... Tonight I trimmed as usual, slicing any stems larger than a dime thickness. Then for the first time I did blanch 3 medium-sized bunches for 5 minutes in boiling water on the stovetop, prior to a brief sauté in EVOO. Made a HUGE difference in the taste - delish, but without that undernote of bitterness. Won't skip that boiling water step again.

So good. I cut off the thick stems, par-boiled the broccoli about 5 min., added garlic and oil and some minced onion to a sauté pan added the broccoli and cooked until tender. After removing from pan added some parm cheese. Perfect.

Delicious! I usually hate Broccoli Rabe and I couldn't stop eating this.

I love making this. Last night, ended up doing some experimenting as well. Fried up some bacon while the b.r. was boiling. Removed the bacon when it was *almost* to the point we like it, and then sauteed chopped garlic and onion in the bacon grease. Added the drained b.r. to the pan and sauteed. When the b.r. was just about done, added the bacon back and finished cooking everything. Added the parm while in the pan and mixed up a bit then served with extra on the side. can't wait to do this again!

I grew up eating Broccoli Rabe (I just call it "Rabe") and as a youngster, wasn't such a big fan of it because it IS BITTER!!! 
 However, there is hope, if you want to try it. First of all, you really need to blanch it for 5 minutes. It takes away the bitterness and it's quite tasty! I usually add a can of tomatoes or just cut some up (if I have canned on hand, I use it, otherwise, I just grab some out of the garden). Use however much garlic you like. I like lots of it, so I'm heavy-handed with it. I brown the garlic, add the steamed rabe, and some cut up vegetarian sausage. If you use real pork sausage, then make sure it is cooked THOROUGHLY!!!! While the rabe is cooking with the garlic and sausage, I toss in a bit of vegetarian broth, the tomatoes and cover it for about 15 minutes. While the rabe is going with the tomatoes and sausage, cook up some pasta. Spaghetti, linguine or penne work well with this. Mix everything together after the pasta is cooked, top with lots of Parmesan cheese and dig in!

I made this recipe with half of the oil and with broccolini as I figured out way too late that I had gotten the wrong type of broccoli. Still, the outcome was very, very good. Will make it again and hopefully I manage to get rapi some time soon.
I love garlic and Parmesan so I'd add onto those measures by taste myself, but I love the recipe. Thank you.
This is my go to recipe for broccoli rabe. Have used this recipe many times over the years.
Where can I buy it? im in the North East Midlands

Followed the recipe to the T and it turned out perfect! Not sure why cutting the X in the bottom of the stems was necessary but I did it and will continue to do so in the future. We love bitter greens and now that I know to cook Rabe, I will be adding this to our meals a lot in the future. Thanks Maria!
I can like broccoli rabe again! Followed recipe and was very good. This is the way to make it.
